scenes.say: For in-scope businesses below fifty million dirhams in revenue, e-invoicing must be implemented by the first of July, twenty twenty-seven. If a new system will send those invoices, that's your end date.

In this hypothetical plan for a trading business, design runs to January and data migration to March, when the provider is appointed. Testing takes April, May is a parallel close of the April books, and June is kept as buffer.

captions_expanded.linkedin:
Oracle implementation time depends on scope, entities and the state of your data, so we'd start from the date the system has to work and plan backwards.

For many businesses that date is set by e-invoicing. In-scope businesses with revenue below AED 50m must appoint an ASP by 31 March 2027 and implement e-invoicing by 1 July 2027 (Ministerial Decision No. 244 of 2025, Art. 5(1)(b); mof.gov.ae, checked 2 Nov 2026).

Hypothetical example, a trading business:
Design to January → data migration to March, ASP appointed → testing, e-invoicing included, in April → a parallel close of the April books in May → June kept as buffer.

That timeline is our view, not a promised duration.

captions_expanded.facebook:
An ERP project is easier to plan from the end date than from the start date.

If a new system will send your e-invoices, it has to work by 1 July 2027 for in-scope businesses below AED 50m (Ministerial Decision No. 244 of 2025; mof.gov.ae, checked 2 Nov 2026).

In our hypothetical example, that leaves design to January, data to March, testing in April, a parallel close in May and June as buffer. Tighter than it looks.
